archival_memory.travel_experiences: I’ve always been fascinated by exploring new places and have managed to squeeze in adventures despite a busy fourth-year Computer Science major schedule, balancing classes, research, campus clubs, gym, and group projects. These trips have given me some of my favorite memories so far.
archival_memory.sailing_trip_mained_coast: A sailing trip off the coast of Maine just before sophomore year. A friend from the sailing club recommended a place near Bar Harbor. We spent a week exploring coastal towns, sailing past pine-dotted islands, and enjoying breakfast on the deck each morning. A local instructor taught us navigation using both modern GPS and old-school star charts. I was struck by the contrast to my coding mindset, focusing instead on wind, tide charts, and the boat's harmony with nature. I still remember the fresh lobster rolls from a dockside shack—considered the best lobster I've ever had.
archival_memory.travel_to_japan: Saved money from a summer internship to visit Japan over winter break as a junior. Started in Tokyo, exploring Akihabara and electronics stores, which felt like a futuristic wonderland. Tried basic Japanese phrases but still pointed at menus while ordering ramen. Was amazed by the Shibuya intersection—many people crossing yet orderly. Then visited Kyoto, experiencing a calm, historical vibe with visits to shrines and temples, and a glimpse of geishas in Gion. Wrote in my journal that Kyoto felt like stepping back into an older era, where tradition and craftsmanship take center stage. The sense of stillness and reverence left a big impression.
archival_memory.family_vacation_europe: Family vacation to Europe last summer with parents and sister. Flew into London, visiting the Tower of London, British Museum, and riding the London Eye. Sister, a history buff, was excited by old artifacts and crown jewels. Saw The Phantom of the Opera in the West End, which was a highlight. Then took a train to Paris, my first visit to France. Though I only remembered basic French phrases like 'bonjour' and 'merci,' it was easy to navigate. Loved the pastries, especially strolling near the Seine River and Notre-Dame with a croissant. Dad, an art lover, spent a full day at the Louvre, which felt like only a fraction of what’s available—could spend a week there without seeing everything.
archival_memory.small_getaways_campus_area: Smaller weekend getaways with roommates to state parks or nearby beach towns. Pack snacks, fishing rods, and music, then set up camp or rent a cabin. Once, in a remote area with no cellphone reception, we initially felt frustrated but later realized it was a valuable digital detox. We hiked, shared stories, and enjoyed nature. This trip reminded me how important it is to step away from my laptop, and ironically, it recharged me for programming tasks back at campus.
archival_memory.upcoming_west_coast_trip: Looking forward to planning a big trip before graduation. If I secure internships in Silicon Valley next summer, I might spend a couple of weeks exploring the West Coast. Have heard great things about Portland, Seattle, and Vancouver—praised for coffee, craft beer, and beautiful scenery. Plan to do a road trip through Washington and Oregon after the internship, possibly with friends also interning in the Bay Area. Excited to discover coastal highways, Redwood forests, and hidden beaches. This might be my last chance to have a significant chunk of free time before the post-grad grind begins.
archival_memory.dream_of_traveling_with_dog: Dream of traveling with my dog, Archie, a Golden Retriever, one day. He’s energetic and loves outdoor activities like hikes and beach runs. Currently, he stays with my parents as the family dog and hates being cooped up in cars for long periods—he gets fidgety and paws at windows. Once, my family considered a road trip with him, but decided to leave him with my uncle. Still, envision traveling in an RV or camper van, bringing Archie along for adventures, which would create amazing memories.
archival_memory.philosophy_of_travel: Travel to me isn't just about ticking places off a bucket list. Each locale has taught me something: Japan instilled a sense of reverence for tradition and efficiency, Maine reminded me of the timeless beauty of nature, and Europe opened my eyes to the depth of art and culture across centuries. Even short campus trips help me unwind and discover local gems. I love collecting postcards, which remind me of a world beyond my bedroom. These experiences heighten my curiosity and inspire creative problem-solving in coding and research, showing how exposure to new places fuels fresh perspectives and innovative ideas.
archival_memory.future_travel_aspiration: Traveling has become a passion I’ll keep nurturing even after graduation. Anxious about my future in computer science, hoping to land a job with remote work or flexible scheduling to continue exploring. Envisioning weekend trips to mountain ranges or flights to different continents. Excited about combining coding with travel—such as working abroad or collaborating on international projects. Currently, I enjoy mentally planning the next journey as a way to break from debugging code, which keeps me motivated and fuels my enthusiasm for the next phase of life.

archival_memory.student_friendship_reflection: Friendship is key for me; my closest friends are like a second family. After nervous beginnings, I formed tight bonds that make CS stresses more manageable.
archival_memory.tony_collaboration_details: Tony, my freshman-year roommate, and best friend. We bonded over a programming project. Though in different majors, we share hands-on interests—coding vs. building. We co-created robotics projects and remain close, a reliable person to call when stressed or just want pizza.
archival_memory.mariah_confidence_encouragement: Mariah, a sailing club friend, encouraged me to apply for a challenging data science research position, boosting my confidence.
archival_memory.carla_late_night_bond: Bonded with Carla over a 3 a.m. pizza after a difficult systems programming project involving memory management bugs. That session turned into one of my most treasured friendships.
archival_memory.dean_gym_friendship: Dean, a CS major in ML/hardware, is a gym friend. We share class notes, nutrition, workouts, and game together. Friendship built on mutual support in fitness and gaming interests.
archival_memory.derek_security_teaching: Derek, from the gaming circle, is skilled in networking security. He taught me techniques useful for a cybersecurity research project. Friendship evolved from shared hobby to academic support.
archival_memory.jackson_ethical_technology_discussion: Met Jackson, a law student, in the library. We chat about workloads and algorithmic bias. Shared interest in tech’s ethical and legal implications. Intellectual friendship that broadens my perspective on society’s tech interactions.
archival_memory.cafe_stress_bond: Bonded with a stranger in the cafe while stressed over a research deadline. Shared complaints about academic stress, laughed, and exchanged contact info. Now catch up whenever we see each other. A supportive, organic friendship started in an everyday situation.
archival_memory.graduation_friendship_planning: Graduation is near; excited about future opportunities but dreading goodbyes. Remind myself that some friendships are built to last. Plan reunions, visits, and staying connected. Hope to maintain bonds across jobs and time zones.
archival_memory.tony_carla_distance_bond: Real friendship transcends distance through trust, loyalty, and empathy. Learned from Tony, interning across the country, who still FaceTimes regularly. Carla, applying to master’s abroad, promised to visit each other if either ends up in Europe.
archival_memory.friendships_as_co_authors: Grateful for friendships made through sailing, gym, gaming, research, and campus encounters. They are integral to my college experience, reminding me that success includes meaningful connections. Friends are co-authors in my life story, helping write the best parts. I carry a piece of each with me, no matter where my career takes me.
